q104a81af.chapter: Ch. 7 What Kind of a Human Being Do You Want?
q104a81af.note: Attribution pass 2: wikiquote/goodreads place it in No Way Out, Ch. 7 ('The fact is that we don't want to be free. What is responsible for our problems is the fear of losing what we have and what we know.'). U.G. speaking.

q69a4a09e.note: Attribution pass 2: well.com (ugbio4.htm) places it in Mahesh Bhatt's biography, Ch. 4, where U.G. tells J. Krishnamurti 'I have wasted seven years listening to you' before leaving for New York; The Mystique of Enlightenment Part One (well.com mystiq1.htm) and Wikipedia give the shorter 'I've wasted seven years'. U.G.'s own recollection of the 1953 break, as quoted by Bhatt; paraphrase ('him' for 'you').

q55779bfa.note: Attribution pass 2: markwhitwell.medium.com places it in Mark Whitwell's interview 'Understanding U.G. Krishnamurti, Part 4', Whitwell recalling U.G.'s view on diet (with U.G.'s radio remark that the body would know what to do even with sawdust and glue). Second-hand wording recorded by Mark Whitwell; no book.

qba6902b4.note: Attribution pass 2: attested only in Mark Whitwell's memoir 'My Life with U.G. Krishnamurti' (Medium) as an oral remark ('Meditation is evil. It is a hoax pulled on humanity...'); the printed near-variant 'meditation is itself an evil' is Mind is a Myth Ch. I. Recorded by Mark Whitwell.

qa86cd51d.note: Attribution pass 2: well.com SWAN_SONG.htm and the Medium transcription place the long wording ('The demand for permanence - permanent relationships, permanent happiness, and permanent bliss - in any field and in any area of human existence is the cause of human misery') in U.G.'s Swan Song, dictated to Louis Brawley in mid-February 2007. Goodreads/quotefancy carry a shorter variant.

q87a66997.note: Attribution pass 2: wikisource and well.com (mystiq4.htm) place it verbatim in The Mystique of Enlightenment, Part Four (conversations 1972-1980): 'the teacher you are running after and the stuff you are thinking about - that's the very thing that must go. Your teacher must go, it doesn't matter who the teacher is.' U.G. speaking.

qfc5867cf.book: talk: First and Last Public Talk of U.G. after his Calamity (Bangalore 1972)
qfc5867cf.note: Attribution pass 2: well.com Talk.htm places it in U.G.'s 1972 Bangalore public talk (the only public talk after the 'calamity'), questioner Mr. Kothari: 'Q: What is the secret of total happiness? U.G.: There is no happiness. Total happiness is an invention. Mr. Kothari: Invention of the mind, you mean? U.G.: There is no mind.' The inner-quest.org UG_Natural_State.htm page reproduces the same transcript. Not one of the published books.

qea825286.chapter: Ch. 8 The Build-Up of Sex and Love
qea825286.note: Attribution pass 2: wikisource places the source passage in No Way Out, Ch. 8: 'sex ... is just a simple biological need of the living organism ... we have turned the basic biological functioning of the body into a pleasure movement.' Paraphrase; U.G. speaking. Also on Goodreads work 43411143 and the-natural-state.blogspot (Amsterdam 1983-84).

qff9ae05a.note: Attribution pass 2: well.com SWAN_SONG.htm and the Medium transcription place it in U.G.'s Swan Song ('the body knows what it needs to do to survive; if it lacks the means to survive, it goes gracefully'), dictated to Louis Brawley, mid-February 2007. Also reproduced on inner-quest.org UG_Words.htm.

qc60032ad.chapter: Book Three: What the Press and Others Say About U.G.
qc60032ad.note: Attribution pass 2: well.com ntbook3.htm is K. Chandrasekhar's compilation 'What the Press and Others Say About U.G.', Book Three of Stopped in Our Tracks. NOT U.G.'s own sentence: a press/commentator paraphrase of his position ('it is through this constant thinking that we are maintaining the continuity of what we call the I or self'). Nearest U.G. text is Thought is Your Enemy (continuity of thought snapped).

q9a924078.note: Attribution pass 2: Goodreads work 43411143 ('Love : Love implies division, separation...') is the only host of this passage ('We are trying to bridge this gap ... with this fancy idea that there must be love between these two individuals'); no canonical book found. Nearest primary text No Way Out Ch. 8. U.G. speaking.

q4fc99cde.note: Attribution pass 2: wikiquote places the source line in The Courage to Stand Alone: 'everything you are doing to be at peace with yourself is what is destroying the peace that is already there.' Paraphrase; a related 'there is already peace in man' passage is in Mind is a Myth Ch. V (wikisource). U.G. speaking.
